name: Image Complexity
description: More complex images (e.g., high detail, cluttered scenes) likely take longer to analyse *both* by the human and the classifier. This is the most likely explanation for distinct groups – images falling into different complexity levels. The classifier might struggle with complex features, while the human needs more time to parse them.  A strong initial factor to investigate.

name: Target Size/Scale
description: Smaller targets in images, or objects viewed from further away, might lead to longer processing times for both the classifier (feature detection) and the human (identification). Different size ranges will create separate timing groups.  This is closely linked to image complexity.

name: Lighting Conditions
description: Poor lighting (low light, glare, shadows) can significantly impact image quality and analysis time.  A classifier might misidentify features, requiring re-analysis. Humans similarly struggle with poor images.  Different lighting scenarios (e.g., direct sunlight, overcast, twilight) could be distinct groups.

name: Object Density
description: The number of objects within the image. More objects means more computation for the classifier and more effort for the human analyst to review. Sparse images vs. crowded images would likely have different processing times.

name: Object Class
description: The *type* of object being imaged. The onboard classifier may be better trained to recognize certain objects than others, creating distinct performance groups. Humans may also have varying expertise with different object types.

name: Image Angle/Viewpoint
description: The angle at which the image is taken. Certain viewpoints may obscure features, making object recognition harder for both systems. Orthographic vs. oblique views will lead to differences.

name: Altitude/Distance to Target
description: The UAV's altitude influences image resolution and target size. Higher altitudes mean lower resolution/smaller targets, increasing analysis time.  Correlated to Target Size.

name: Weather Conditions
description: Rain, fog, snow, or haze can degrade image quality and introduce noise, affecting both classification and human analysis.  This is related to lighting but represents an atmospheric effect.

name: Classifier Confidence Threshold
description: The onboard classifier might have an internal confidence threshold. Images where the classifier is near the threshold could trigger re-analysis, creating a distinct group. This is a system parameter.

name: Human Operator Fatigue
description: The human analyst's alertness and concentration level can fluctuate over time, affecting analysis speed. This could create a time-dependent grouping.

name: UAV Vibration/Motion Blur
description: Excessive vibration during flight, or rapid UAV movements, can cause motion blur, decreasing image quality and increasing analysis time.

name: Background Clutter
description: A complex background can make it harder to distinguish the target object, increasing processing time for both the classifier and the human.

name: Image Resolution
description: While potentially controlled, variations in the achieved image resolution (due to sensor settings or focus) can influence analysis time. Higher resolution = more data.

name: Time of Day
description: Changing sunlight angles throughout the day influence image quality. Similar to lighting, but tied to time.

name: GPS Accuracy/Waypoint Precision
description: If the UAV doesn't accurately reach the waypoints, images might be slightly off-angle or have unexpected framing, affecting analysis.
